intro.say: Birds are amazing! Let's find out what all birds have.

rounds.say: Every bird has feathers, two wings, two legs and a beak. Feathers keep birds warm and help them fly.
rounds.caption: Feathers · Wings · Beak

rounds.say: All birds hatch from eggs. Many birds build nests to keep their eggs safe and warm.
rounds.caption: Birds hatch from eggs

options.label: Fur
options.why: Fur is for mammals like bears.

options.label: Scales
options.why: Fish have scales.

options.label: Dog
options.why: A dog has fur.

options.label: Fish
options.why: A fish has fins.

rounds.explain: An owl has feathers, wings and a beak. It is a bird!

rounds.ask: How many legs does a bird have?

options.why: Cats and dogs have 4 legs. Birds have 2.
Insects have 6 legs.

rounds.ask: What does a baby bird hatch from?

options.label: A nut
options.why: Squirrels love nuts, but chicks come from eggs.

options.label: A flower
options.why: Bees visit flowers.

rounds.explain: Baby birds peck their way out of eggs.

rounds.ask: What does a bird use to pick up food?

options.label: Hands
options.why: Birds don't have hands.

options.label: Ears
options.why: Ears are for hearing.

rounds.explain: Birds use their beaks to pick up and eat food.

intro.say: A bird's beak is a tool for eating. Different birds have different beaks!

rounds.say: An eagle has a hooked beak to tear meat. A parrot has a strong beak to crack nuts. A duck has a flat beak to scoop food from water.
rounds.caption: Hook · Nutcracker · Scoop

rounds.say: Birds build nests from twigs, grass, mud and feathers. They lay eggs and sit on them to keep them warm.
rounds.caption: Building a nest

rounds.ask: Which bird has a strong beak for cracking nuts?

options.label: Duck
options.why: A duck's flat beak scoops food from water.

options.label: Swan
options.why: Swans eat water plants.

rounds.explain: A parrot's strong curved beak can crack hard nuts.

rounds.ask: An eagle has a sharp hooked beak. What does it eat?

options.label: Nectar
options.why: Nectar is a sweet drink for long thin beaks.

options.label: Grass
options.why: Eagles are hunters.

rounds.explain: A hooked beak tears meat. Eagles hunt small animals.

rounds.ask: Which of these could a bird use to build a nest?

options.label: Bricks
options.why: Bricks are much too heavy!

options.label: Big rocks
options.why: Big rocks are too heavy to carry.

rounds.explain: Birds carry small twigs and grass to weave their nests.

rounds.ask: Put the bird's story in order.
rounds.explain: First the nest, then the eggs, then keeping them warm, and then the chicks hatch!

rounds.ask: A duck has a flat beak. Where does it find its food?

options.label: Up in trees
options.why: Ducks look for food in water.

options.label: In the desert
options.why: A desert has no water for ducks.

rounds.explain: A duck scoops up water plants and tiny animals with its flat beak.

intro.say: Most birds fly, but not all of them! Let's find out what really makes a bird a bird.

rounds.say: A penguin can't fly, but it is a super swimmer. An ostrich can't fly either, but it runs very fast. It is the biggest bird of all!
rounds.caption: Not all birds fly

rounds.say: Some birds fly far away to warm places in winter, where there is more food. This long trip is called migration.
rounds.caption: Migration

options.label: They all fly
options.why: Penguins and ostriches can't fly.

options.label: They all swim
options.why: Most birds can't swim like penguins.

rounds.explain: Every bird has feathers. No other animal alive today has them!

rounds.ask: A butterfly has wings and can fly. Is it a bird?

options.label: Yes
options.why: Wings are not enough. Birds have feathers.

rounds.explain: A butterfly has no feathers. It is an insect with 6 legs.

rounds.ask: Which bird swims well but can't fly?

options.label: Eagle
options.why: Eagles soar high in the sky.

options.label: Owl
options.why: Owls fly silently at night.

rounds.explain: Penguins use their wings like flippers to swim.

rounds.ask: Why do some birds fly away when winter comes?

options.label: For a party
options.why: It's a long trip for a reason.

options.label: To sleep
options.why: They need food, not just sleep.

rounds.explain: In winter food is hard to find, so they fly to warmer places.

rounds.ask: Owls can see well in the dark. When do most owls hunt?

options.label: At midday
options.why: Most owls sleep in the day.

options.label: Only in rain
options.why: Rain doesn't matter much.

rounds.explain: Owls hunt at night, when mice come out.

rounds.ask: Bird or not a bird? Look for feathers!
rounds.explain: Penguins, turkeys and swans have feathers. Butterflies, bees and squirrels don't.
